title: Ventura Analytics - Pilot Econ Weekly Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review tokens-per-dollar results, discuss caching and batching tradeoffs, and align on next steps. Redwood to run extended benchmark with KV/prefix caching and provide updated pricing for dedicated sizing. Customer to share traffic sample and prompt set for final tuning.
next_steps: Redwood to run 24h tokens-per-dollar benchmark with prefix caching enabled and share raw CSV + summary (Diego)
Ventura to provide 7-day production traffic sample and top 200 prompt variations (Priya)
Maya to send dedicated sizing + updated pricing and pilot contract draft
Schedule infra deep-dive (SE + Ventura infra) for next Wednesday
action_items: Diego Alvarez - run 24h tokens-per-dollar benchmark with KV/prefix caching + 95th percentile latency report - 2026-03-25
Priya Menon - upload anonymized 7-day traffic sample and prompt set to shared S3 (link provided) - 2026-03-22
Maya Chen - email updated pricing for dedicated pools and pilot contract draft + share Redwood security one-pager - 2026-03-20
Samir Patel - confirm VPC peering feasibility and firewall rules, note any internal SLAs - 2026-03-24
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. quick check, is this still 13:30 PT? cool. we'll keep it tight 45 minutes ish.
[00:12] Priya Menon: Yep this time works. Focus today: tokens per dollar numbers, that caching experiment you ran and batching impact, okay?
[00:20] Maya Chen: Exactly. Diego will walk through the 48-hour run and then we'll talk tradeoffs. Diego over to you.

[00:27] Diego Alvarez: Hey all. quick context—ran two 48-hour passes on the pilot workload. baseline was hosted small model variant, no caching, request-level batching at 8ms window. then we enabled KV prefix caching and increased batching to 32 tokens window for throughput tests.

[00:47] Diego Alvarez: Results summary — baseline tokens per dollar ~ 1.8k tokens / $; with KV prefix caching we saw effective tokens per dollar jump to ~3.5k, so roughly 1.9x improvement. when we increase batching it pushes to 4.1k but tail latency goes up 25-30% at 95th percentile.
[01:10] Samir Patel: Real quick — when you say KV prefix caching, you're caching the model KV for repeated prompts or cached prefixes?

[01:17] Diego Alvarez: good q. it's prefix caching for common prompt starts — so the KV cache avoids recomputing first N tokens, particularly in our use case where templates are reused. occasionally the transcriber says "kayv cash" — but yeah it's KV cache.
[01:30] Lena Ortiz: That matches our traffic — ~60% of requests share the same opening template. curious about cold-starts and cache invalidation though.

[01:39] Diego Alvarez: Cold-start penalty was minimal in steady-state; however when we tested with synthetic bursts that had a lot of unique prefixes, cache hit rate dropped and tokens/$ benefit shrank to about 1.2x. so caching helps when reuse is high.
[02:05] Priya Menon: And batching — Diego you said latency spike. what's the P99 move? we're sensitive to P99 due to user interactive flows.

[02:12] Diego Alvarez: P99 increases by roughly 40% when hand-tuning batching for throughput (the 32 window). P95 goes up ~25%. median unchanged. So it depends on how tolerant your UI is. we can do adaptive batching to keep short-tail latency but still get some cost gains.

[02:30] Maya Chen: Just to frame: Adaptive batching lets us have small windows for low in-flight but accumulate when load is higher. That keeps interactive latencies acceptable while improving tokens/$ during busy periods.
[02:42] Samir Patel: Have you tested with dedicated capacity? For predictable throughput we might prefer dedicated GPUs — how do the economics change versus hosted?

[02:50] Diego Alvarez: Good point. We did a sizing pass — for your 150 rps peak the estimate for a single dedicated pool (N4-ish) gives better steady tokens/$ once utilization is high. But the reserved cost upfront means the breakeven depends on sustained utilization. I put conservative numbers in the shared sheet.
[03:07] Priya Menon: Can you share that sheet again? the one with tokens/sec, hourly cost and amortized GPU pricing?
[03:12] Maya Chen: link: https://app.redwood.ai/pilot/ventura/benchmarks (shared). i'll also email a CSV export after the call.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: On security: we need SOC2 docs and audit log retention detail for the pilot. also around data residency — some customers require EU only.

[03:28] Maya Chen: Noted. i'll attach the SOC2 summary and the security one-pager. for pilot we can toggle retention to 30 days, and for production you can opt for VPC + KMS integration. i'll add that to the action items.

[03:40] Diego Alvarez: Back to technical: a couple of caveats — our caching experiment assumes deterministic prompts; if you do heavy tool-calling or function-outputs that mutate context often, cache hit rates drop. also long context lengths reduce effective batch size improvements.
[03:58] Priya Menon: Our workflows include some long-context summarization, but the high-volume paths are short Q&A. so maybe hybrid is fine.

[04:06] Diego Alvarez: Exactly. For hybrid traffic we recommend: 1) prefix caching for templated flows, 2) small batch windows for interactive, and 3) background bulk queue for async jobs to use high-batch windows.
[04:24] Samir Patel: On the benchmark: can you include tokenization differences across model variants? some of our older prompts tokenize differently and can skew tokens/$.
[04:31] Diego Alvarez: yes will include tokenization breakdown per model. also we'll give a per-route cost map so you can see the hot endpoints.
[04:40] Maya Chen: Quick pause — anyone seeing audio issues? otherwise we'll keep rolling. (brief chuckle) Lena no issues?
[04:46] Lena Ortiz: all good here.
[04:50] Diego Alvarez: Another datapoint — cache warmup time averages 2-4 minutes depending on request fanout. in one experiment we saw 15% lower early-run efficiency until warmup completed.
[05:02] Priya Menon: that's acceptable. our usage bursts are usually >10min.

[05:08] Maya Chen: On the dedicated vs hosted pricing: i'll send two scenarios — low utilization (less than 30%) and high utilization. dedicated becomes attractive at ~60% sustained utilization in your workload per our model.
[05:20] Samir Patel: what about fallback policies? if dedicated pool is saturated do you auto-fall back to hosted and what happens to the cache?

[05:28] Diego Alvarez: Redwood supports smart routing — we can fail over to hosted-compatible model variants. cache won't carry over, but we can route similar customer traffic to the same region to retain warm caches where possible.
[05:40] Priya Menon: Any notes on quantization or model variants? we have some quality constraints.

[05:44] Diego Alvarez: We recommend 4-bit quantized variants for cost sensitive routes, but run your regeneration evals — quality delta is small for short answers but larger for nuanced summarization. we can include suggested prompt-sensitivity tests in the deliverable.
[05:56] Maya Chen: let's surface that in the next deliverable: tokens/$ + quality heatmap by route.
[06:03] Lena Ortiz: good.
[06:06] [10:12] Priya Menon: (background) sorry ran into a call, back now — what's the biggest risk for us in the next two weeks?

[06:14] Maya Chen: I'd say three risks — cache hit rate lower than expected, insufficient sustained utilization to justify dedicated, and any unexpected security signoffs. we will mitigate with the 24h benchmark, your traffic sample, and the security packet.
[06:30] Diego Alvarez: on the benchmark we'll include synthetic bursts + long-tail traffic to stress the cache and batching knobs so you can see worst-case and steady-state numbers.
[06:40] Samir Patel: For the 24h run — can you also produce a per-minute tokens/sec graph and an annotated CSV? our infra needs to map that to instance autoscale events.
[06:47] Diego Alvarez: yes will include per-minute CSV + annotated events and P95/P99 columns.
[06:55] Maya Chen: Next — procurement. Maya: any updates on pilot contract?
[07:00] Maya Chen: We have a pilot template. i'll attach the draft with options for month-to-month vs 3-month commit. pricing differs; i'll put two line items in the doc.
[07:08] Priya Menon: procurement will want cancellation clauses and data deletion specifics — can you add that?
[07:12] Maya Chen: absolutely, will include data deletion SLA and export procedures.
[07:18] Diego Alvarez: One more note on batching — adaptive batching requires a little more runtime instrumentation but we can flip it on/off without redeploying models.
[07:28] Samir Patel: perfect. that lowers risk for us.
[07:32] Maya Chen: ok wrapping to action items — Diego will run the 24h KV caching benchmark, Priya uploads traffic sample, Samir confirms VPC rules, i will send pricing + SOC2 docs. any objections?
[07:45] Priya Menon: no objections. also can you include a short list of recommended prompt edits to improve tokenization efficiency?
[07:52] Diego Alvarez: yes, we'll add a "token efficiency" checklist—trimming stopwords in fixed templates, prefer shorter slot names, etc.
[08:00] Lena Ortiz: can you bump the next sync to same time next week? we'll invite procurement and infra leads.
[08:06] Maya Chen: scheduled tentatively. i'll send calendar invite once pricing doc is out.
[08:12] [47:58] Maya Chen: cool thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the thread. meeting adjourned.
[48:00] End of recording
